Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

dsOMOPClient 2.10.4 (2026-11-13)

  • Corrected: assigned age bands, birth-year bands and panel/calendar categories use the controlled factor reconciliation even when concept-label translation is disabled. Re-run recipes against the corrected server to recreate factors with shared levels; explicit numeric date representations remain numeric.

Date presentation (A-28 / CR-29)

  • Corrected (DATES-B4): year-bearing custom factors include every year in a declared level_range, including unused middle years and ISO boundary weeks. Empty inputs stay empty, including patterns with literal separators. Empty or disjoint observed dates no longer cause valid public keys to refuse publication. Re-execute affected recipes; no declaration changes are needed.

  • Corrected (DATES-B1–B3): native date reducers and raw date columns apply the effective invalid/domain/future policy after selection and before presentation. A selected date beyond as_of becomes NA; no earlier event is substituted. Yearless custom factors use first appearance in exactly 2000–2399, and escaped percent directives are literal text in validation, rendering and label keys. Re-execute affected recipes to refresh values and ordered-factor contrasts; no declaration changes are needed. Active %Y-W%V remains refused: use %G-W%V.

  • Newly permitted: omop_date_spec(), omop_date(), omop_date_components(), omop_date_parts(), omop_time_between() and omop_age_at() compose native calendar dates, periods, partial dates, date parts and independently anchored ages. Variable fields override recipe defaults. Calendar, fiscal, ISO/CDC and explicitly profiled epi weeks support ordered factors, numeric coordinates and inclusive period bounds. English names and validated custom patterns are locale independent. Date factors reconcile through the existing controlled factor transport, including public zero-count categories.

  • Corrected: exact-date assignment needs no dsomop.allow_absolute_dates setting. All date-derived forms retain class-2 provenance, and publication, protected lineage and aggregate admission remain enforced. Native presentation cannot be erased by an omitted legacy date policy. Numeric measures stay numeric. Legacy first_date/last_date offsets and omop_age() annual ages keep their existing meaning when the new APIs are absent.

  • Newly refused: unsafe/custom patterns (use %G-W%V for ISO weeks), incomplete epi profiles, irrelevant spec fields, duplicate part names and overlapping explicit legacy/native date policies. Express native policies in date_spec. Formats without a roster date slot refuse a date variable rather than encoding a Date/factor into a numeric sparse matrix.

  • Migration: replace fixed-anchor offsets plus mutate()/cut() with omop_date("first_visit", omop_date_spec(precision="quarter")); replace annual ages with omop_age_at("death") for completed years. Incomplete birth dates give NA unless an explicit imputation or unit="annual_years" is chosen. Coarsened labels are ordered factors; request representation="number" for trends or "start"/"end" for Date bounds. Native interval/panel/survival endpoint columns are added alongside unchanged internal day offsets when a recipe date spec requests presentation.

Concept labels and categorical outputs

  • Corrected: concept-valued outputs are unordered factors by semantic type, including renamed reducers, dictionaries and staged components. Vocabulary labels and generated names reconcile by concept ID across retained sites; absent categories retain their declared levels. Presentation-only requests may use different vocabulary versions. Computation continues to use IDs.
  • Newly permitted: labels and column_names maps on omop_variable() and omop_recipe(), with variable maps taking precedence. Equal concept labels deliberately merge categories; column names must be unique valid R names. Use options = list(translate_concepts = FALSE) for numeric concept IDs and untranslated generated names. Ordinary age/calendar categories still reconcile.
  • Newly permitted: ds.omop.table(data, column, conns) pools concept counts while preserving the complete permitted category contract, including unused zero-count levels and labels containing commas. Failed or suppressed site counts are never filled with zeros. Actual missing values stay missing.
  • Corrected: concept model frames retain shared levels during subsetting. CSV staging distinguishes literal "NA" and leading backslashes from missing values through the descriptor’s backslash-v1 encoding. Consumers must use the descriptor-aware reader. Existing descriptors retain legacy decoding.
  • Newly refused: malformed/empty label maps, colliding explicit column names, translation with factor_concepts = FALSE, and servers lacking the concept presentation capability. Remove that flag or disable translation explicitly; use matching 2.10.4 packages for the new presentation contract. Reconciliation failures roll back all sites and cannot be bypassed with small-site skipping.

Native execution and compatibility

  • Corrected: native outputs and reducers complete the integrated language-2 path, preserving BIGINT values for empty/all-NULL streams, population membership, interval coverage, survival censoring and panel source identity. Concept reconciliation retains authenticated person lineage and snapshot provenance when resealing. Final publication and aggregate gates still apply.
  • Corrected: v1 lowering retains supported legacy empty populations, owned cohort references, output shapes and score semantics in the compatibility layer. Native v2 keeps explicit coverage, anchors, censoring and grain rules. Unsupported or ambiguous forms fail with a typed reason; use explicit native declarations when migrating. See the population and extraction vignettes.

Upgrading from 2.10.3

Install dsOMOP and dsOMOPClient 2.10.4 together, publish dsOMOP’s methods and Options on Opal, and check ds.omop.server.version(). Existing valid secrets are reused automatically; no privacy setting, state provisioning, epoch bump, ETL hook or TLS change is needed. Re-execute recipes to recreate categorical columns. Use as.character() for factor labels, never numeric factor codes for arithmetic. Legacy date offsets and annual omop_age() retain their meaning; choose the native date/age helpers explicitly for new semantics. The protected release protocol introduced in 2.10.3 is unchanged; pooling still requires compatible contracts and logical source identities.

Release verification: recipe/publication contract run 43515122503 passed fresh and upgrade paths on Opal 5.7.6 and 6.1.3; full e2e run 43515127555 passed both fresh and upgrade jobs. Both tested harness commit 17e5df40f4718bdece091f68d3003c764f061854. These are evidence for that candidate, not a claim of live execution on every supported SQL dialect.

dsOMOPClient 2.10.3 (2026-11-13)

Pairs with dsOMOP 2.10.3, the security release of the OHDSI-tools audit.

  • Corrected named single-output transport: output mappings and other named scalar arguments now travel as one encoded JSON object, preserving their names without a c()/structure() expression. Single-output recipes and language-2 verbs run under the normal method allowlist; adapter refusals reach the analyst with their actual reason. Existing call syntax is unchanged.

  • Release 2.10.3 pairs both packages, including recipe language 2 and the publication protocol. Existing valid secrets are reused; ordinary operation needs no privacy settings, state provisioning, epoch bump, ETL hook or TLS change. Opal’s installed package and published profile remain distinct; the version check identifies a stale profile. README upgrade notes describe compatible pooling, legacy execution and changed-answer behavior.

  • Corrected upgrade advice for the publication protocol backported to 2.10.3: an installed 2.10.3 with a stale 2.10.2 profile asks to publish its settings, rather than incorrectly requiring a further package upgrade.

  • Protected histogram pooling retains its cells when a distribution gate withholds moments; unavailable means and standard deviations stay NA.

  • New protected-release contract: dsOMOP 2.10.3 servers advertise privacy_contract = "protected_release_fixed_basis_or_realised_v1". ds.omop.dp.release() validates their dsomop-protected-release-v1 payloads (route, guarantee scope, signed components, no private material, no history-dependent fields) and pools them by summing the signed components of compatible sites and deriving each view once. Pooling a federation mixing 2.10.3 servers with per-release servers (2.7.1-2.10.2) is refused; type = "split" retains labelled per-site results. Every pre-2.10.3 server gets a plain upgrade warning: installing this client does not repair its server-side inference defects. The new server explicitly refuses typed status/release preflight from clients 2.10.2 and earlier.

  • Heuristic payloads are never presented as differential privacy: realised_sticky releases report mechanism_epsilon = NA, a warning, and no pooled epsilon; meta$privacy$protection names each site’s route. For fixed-synopsis releases the pooled epsilon is reported for disjoint sites (maximum) and overlapping sites (sum), applying to the declared fixed vectors before exact support gates. It is not an API-transcript guarantee.

  • Standalone typed counts on 2.10.3 servers use the shared person-total allocation (0.2 of the reference calibration) and are noisier than before; typed bounded means need a registered public scale; typed histogram breaks are reported as requested and as effective (public-grid) breaks; a distinct-label cardinality is not pooled across sites.

  • ds.omop.analysis.run() pools protected catalog releases (the release_pooling descriptor of 2.10.3 entries) from their signed components (one row per owner, stratum and interaction view: persons, mean, SD, events, person-time and rate where defined; pooled cells in the cells attribute). It never mixes standard and protected frames. Older clients see these entries as not poolable and display the per-server frames.

  • Printed protection labels describe fixed-synopsis, heuristic realised-contribution and mixed protection and list the fields a server withheld and why.

  • One logical node is never pooled twice: protected typed and catalogue pooling require every site’s public logical source identifier (source$logical_source_id) and refuse a federation in which two connections name the same node, or in which a site’s independence cannot be established (missing identifier). Per-site results stay available with pool = FALSE / type = "split". Equal answers from independent sites still pool; source identity is never inferred from values.

  • Guarantee claims are checked: a heuristic realised-contribution or mixed release (typed payload or catalogue protection label) carrying a finite mechanism or API-transcript epsilon, or a delta, is refused, as is a fixed synopsis without a finite mechanism epsilon and delta 0. Typed payloads and catalogue labels also require a guarantee scope coherent with their protection route, including the protected block of mixed frames. Only fixed synopses are printed with a delta.

  • Typed pooling sums the signed components of the complete registered basis and derives each requested view once. Binary rates carry explicit numerator and denominator masks, including the nonmissing denominator; equal-width domains with different labels cannot pool. Weighted numeric records use one versioned complete-atom projection onto their protected weighted total, so one-site pooling and every displayed rebinning agree with the server.

  • Person-time pooling reconstructs the complete gender, age and year hierarchy before selecting views, preserving parent event, time and capped recurrent totals and both margins of crossed views. Nested Achilles histograms retain their root’s histogram margins. Versioned transportation display keeps converged Dykstra results and uses a deterministic feasible margin repair after its iteration limit; that fallback is not an exact L2 projection. First-event and capped recurrent event-time histograms pool their complete signed day hierarchy, project it onto the person or recurrent event total, then select the requested day, month or year bins. Recurrent persons counts distinct contributors among the same K-capped occurrences using a complete canonical interval-presence vector (sensitivity 3K; fractions N/R .2 each, A/B/C .1 each and P .3); coarse persons are never sums of daily persons. Its versioned feasible radial projection enforces event/person bounds and interval constraints, but retreat toward the event-mass anchor can add bias.

  • Record-weighted protected releases (the eight QueryLibrary record summaries) are pooled by summing the signed persons, records and lattice sums per stratum and deriving the record-weighted mean and SD once (never weighted by persons); sites must share the entry, scale, bounds and cap. Versioned record displays constrain records to [N, K N]. Unscaled value histograms pool their signed cells onto that record total; pooled frames carry value_histograms and value_quantiles attributes with interval and tail-censoring information. A missing per-site histogram remains unavailable.

  • Protected effect estimates (CohortMethod Poisson and grouped-time Cox, interaction estimates, the SCCS incidence rate ratio) are pooled, as in 2.10.2, by inverse-variance meta-analysis of the per-site protected estimates; the signed-component pooling stays in the protected_components attribute. Cox exit-time cells are projected onto the pooled C6 event and non-event parents. Interaction C6/C8 pooling projects the complete signed atomic family before deriving requested subgroup views, retaining both subgroup and arm margins and explicit view identifiers. C8 uses finite IPF plus a feasible margin repair, not an exact KL/L2 projection. Missing or incompatible status/family metadata is refused. Cox cells are never refitted, and SCCS cells are never pooled.

  • Servers without the DP service pool their standard outputs by the established contract; protected and standard frames are never mixed. Pooled standard-mode frames with protected person-time say that those fields are sums of protected values. The moment projection matches the server’s.

  • DP status: snapshot_id is a display label (servers 2.10.3 key fixed synopses on an automatic data generation they never release). Empty, absent or arbitrary display labels never affect protected-client admission.

Recipe language integration

Recipe language 2.0 ships with typed constructors, client validation, v1 compatibility lowering and the server publication protocol. The entries below describe the supported operations and migration paths.

Recipe language 2.0 (WS-8)

  • New language-2 constructors (design section 2): omop_concept_set(), omop_event() with omop_where() / omop_where_tree() row predicates and omop_unit() normalisation, the bounded adapters omop_episode_members() and omop_cost(); criteria omop_has(), omop_has_not(), omop_count_is(), omop_not(), omop_all(), omop_any(), omop_person(), omop_age_is(), omop_observed(), omop_in_cohort(); omop_window(), omop_bound(), omop_anchor(); omop_index(), omop_any_of(), omop_end(), omop_coverage(); omop_era() and omop_censor() (with when_index_source, amendment A-7); omop_reduce() under the frozen reducer contract (including covered_days(coverage =, observed_only =) and supply_days(fills =)); omop_age() (with bands / age_breaks), omop_sex(), omop_race(), omop_ethnicity(), omop_birth_year_band(), omop_died(), omop_days_to_death(), omop_n_observation_periods(), omop_obs_duration(), omop_prior_obs(), omop_followup(), omop_observed_days(), omop_score(), omop_population_column(); omop_match(), omop_age_band(), omop_strata(); recipe_concept_sets(), recipe_import_concept_sets(), recipe_export_concept_sets() and recipe_explain() (its appended symbol names the server handle omopPlanExplainDS() reads).
  • Every 2.10.1 export keeps its positional formals; new arguments are appended: omop_variable(event, reducer, where, visit, broadcast), omop_variable_block(where, visit, concept_col, visit_filter) (F-24; visit_filter is the legacy alias of visit, giving both is an error), omop_population(index, match, coverage), omop_output(rows, grain, columns, format, sources, collapse) (type now defaults to NULL; giving neither type nor format keeps "wide"), omop_recipe(concept_sets, events, intervals, coverage, publish), recipe_execute(on_small_site), ds.omop.plan.execute(on_small_site), recipe_to_plan(version = 2L).
  • recipe_to_plan() emits a v2 plan by default (validated against the vendored plan-v2.json); recipe_to_plan(version = 1) returns the unchanged 2.10.1 plan of a recipe built from 2.10.1 constructors. A recipe built only from 2.10.1 constructors (and without parent_id) executes as that v1 plan, so its results are unchanged, unless the v1 compiler refuses one of the shapes 2.10.3 newly permits (below); such a recipe, and any recipe using language-2 constructs, executes as a v2 plan on servers advertising recipe_language 2 and every operation it needs.
  • The legacy survival, intervals, temporal_covariates and person_period presets lower to their language-2 formats with the legacy defaults (TAR 0 to 730 days, censoring at the observation-period end, at death when censoring$death = TRUE and at the cohort end); a legacy multi-state survival output keeps its v1 plan.
  • omop_where() admits an inline omop_param() placeholder (the only call it evaluates, with literal arguments; A-13).
  • Plan selection (A-14) is one rule for recipe_execute(), recipe_validate(), recipe_preview(), recipe_explain() and recipe_lint(). recipe_explain() of a recipe that executes as its v1 plan explains that v1 payload and its legacy rules (with conns, the server’s lowered IR and digest) and never presents the native rendering as the executed plan. With conns, only the sites whose profile publishes omopPlanExplainDS are asked; the others and every failed call are reported by site, a v1 explanation marks its lowered IR and digest unavailable when no site explained it or the sites disagree, and the execution route (protocol, legacy call or refusal) is stated (review B7). A recipe with neither a v1 plan nor a native rendering is refused naming both causes; native-rendering limitations direct to recipe_to_plan(version = 1).
  • Language-2 plans always carry an explicit publish list: the recipe’s roots, else every declared output; an execution with a partial out publishes exactly the mapped roots.
  • Temporal-covariates and person-period outputs whose variables request different analyses per concept emit per-source analyses (source_analyses, A-14): only the declared (concept, analysis) pairs are computed. A covariates_sparse output, which has no per-source selection, refuses them; options$analyses naming an analysis no variable requests is refused.
  • Names follow A-9: an imported Circe concept set is .sanitize_name(<name>) (fallback concept_set_<CodesetId>); an unnamed event is <concept set>_<table> with exactly five abbreviations (dx, rx, px, lab, obs) and the full table name otherwise; collisions take the first free _2, _3, … without truncating the suffix.
  • The normal form and semantic digest of language-2 plans come from the vendored A-11 normaliser (R/plan_normalize_v2.R), whose grain rule follows the left member of an intersect or setdiff.
  • Language-2 plans execute through the same publication protocol as v1 plans (status, inventory, on_small_site, rollback; see Corrected and Newly permitted), sent losslessly after every server’s recipe-language capabilities are checked; federated v2 executions bind the plan’s semantic digest.
  • print(), recipe_explain() and recipe_lint() state the defaults a recipe relies on: “follow-up ends 730 days after index” for a survival output without tar (F-4, the default is kept), the banded age_group of baseline versus exact age in wide (F-5), the unique/drop/drop coverage of indexed populations, collapse, missing = "skip"; class-2 columns are reported as INFO quasi_identifier; the has_measurement / missing_measurement pair is explained (B-7, unchanged v1 meanings; in v2 omop_has_not(event) = no row, omop_has_not(event, nonmissing = "value_as_number") = no non-null value).
  • Index-relative recency uses days_since / days_until / first_date / last_date reducers with an explicit reference anchor (F-18); time_since keeps its fixed-date meaning.
  • Named events and intervals are declarative (review N1): a declaration may reference one declared after it; a dependency cycle is refused, naming it (a -> b -> a).
  • Population rules are the server’s (S/R/ir_validate.R; review B3). The cases of a match may be any indexed population: an index population, a criteria child of one, or a set operation that A-11 counts as indexed (a union when any member is, intersect and setdiff after their left member). A population used only as a matching controls template may carry an index-referenced omop_age_is(), evaluated at case time; one that is also an output’s rows, a parent, a set-op member or match cases still needs an index. Episode grain over a population without an index is refused by recipe_to_plan().
  • omop_observed(gap = ) with any non-NULL gap, 0 included, needs the server operation population.coverage.union; the client checks it before any assignment (review B2).
  • publish = character(0) (also recipe_set_publish(recipe, character(0))) publishes nothing: the plan carries publish = [] through JSON, YAML, recipe_to_code() and plan files, the servers validate it and report an empty inventory, and execution returns an empty mapping; NULL still means every output (review B6).
  • recipe_export_concept_sets() refuses a nested exclusion (an exclusion with its own exclusion), which an OHDSI concept-set expression cannot carry, instead of flattening it (review B4).
  • ds.omop.server.version() tells an old installation (dsOMOP before 2.10.3, where publishing again cannot add the protocol methods) from an upgraded server whose profile still publishes the old methods (stale publication), and adds the list column recipe_language: each site’s capability block (version, operations, dialect), "unavailable" for a site that predates it and "not connected" without an OMOP session (review N2).

Simple layer, parameters and verbs (WS-9)

  • Simple layer (design section 3): omop_study() returns an ordinary omop_recipe – one indexed population and the requested "baseline" (wide), "survival" (competing_risk with two or more outcomes), "long" (the outcome events) and "panel" (dense 30-day person periods) outputs, all with episode grain, priority ties and relative dates; require entries (prior_observation, followup, age, sex, has, no_history_of, in_cohort, criterion objects) expand one criterion each. print() lists every default the study chose, recipe_explain() states them (INFO simple_layer in recipe_lint()), recipe_to_code() prints the advanced expansion. omop_new_users() is the era-indexed population of first-eligible users after an observed washout. The shortcuts omop_ever(), omop_count(), omop_first_value(), omop_last_value(), omop_mean_value(), omop_min_value(), omop_max_value(), omop_value_at_index(), omop_days_since(), omop_days_until(), omop_first_date(), omop_last_date() and omop_history() return ordinary reducer variables; before, after and window are mutually exclusive and default to any time up to the index date; a numeric unit restricts the unit, omop_unit() converts.
  • Parameters (design section 2.10): omop_param(name, type, default, description) placeholders stand for any language-2 value (integer and number placeholders admit `+ - * /, unary minus and unary plus);recipe_params()lists them and refuses two definitions of one name;recipe_bind()checks each value against its type, substitutes it and rebuilds every object that held a placeholder through its constructor (a recipe may be bound in stages);recipe_to_plan()binds defaults and refuses an unbound parameter. Parametrised recipes round-trip through JSON, YAML andrecipe_to_code()`. Acceptance recipe 13 and its twelve variants bind to their frozen plans.
  • recipe_merge(a, b, prefix = NULL): one shared namespace (a name used by both needs one definition), or every node of b renamed <prefix>_<name> with every reference rewritten (anchors, censoring and its index-source tags, index arms, parents, set operations, match inputs, output rows, columns and dependencies, publication roots); outputs with implicit columns keep exactly their own variables, b’s base population keeps its meaning, block metadata is preserved and parameters are shared by name.
  • The complete set of editing functions is exported: recipe_add_population(), recipe_add_event(), recipe_add_concept_set(), recipe_add_interval(), recipe_add_block(), recipe_add_variable(), recipe_add_filter(), recipe_add_output(), their recipe_remove_*() counterparts, recipe_set_scope(), recipe_set_options() and recipe_set_publish() (2.10.1 formals unchanged).
  • ds.omop.mutate(x, ..., newobj) (design 2.11, 4.6) derives columns from R expressions translated into the closed mutation AST of the vendored mutate-v1.json – columns, literals, `+ - * /, conditions,ifelse(),case_when(),coalesce(),cut()(R'sright = TRUEdefault), date arithmetic -- validated before it is sent and never evaluated;newobj = xcoordinates replacement across sites with verified rollback and retained recovery copies where restoration is uncertain.ds.omop.filter(x, expr = omop_where(…))filters with the closed predicate grammar. Both need the servers to advertiseverb.mutate/verb.filter_expr(dsOMOP 2.10.3);omopMutateDSis a listed server method ofds.omop.server.version()`.

Corrected

  • (A-24) The exact frozen windowed-features corpus fixture #1 has an unindexed base and is unchanged_invalid. Its explicit v1 omitted-grain refusal permits an attempted native rendering, but does not certify that the recipe executes: native rendering and automatic selection refuse with the indexed-population diagnostic before assignment. Root cohort scope alone does not supply an index. A separate indexed, per-variable-window variant defaults to episode grain and passes server semantic validation; its execution regression remains gated on native compiler integration.

  • (WS-9 review B1–B2; A-23) Standalone verb assignments include commit verification in their transaction. Fresh outputs are removed on every site after a verification failure. In-place mutations restore every possibly written site, including a site with a lost acknowledgement; recovery copies remain where restoration cannot be confirmed. Errors distinguish unresolved recovery, failed cleanup and a mutation that has already committed.

  • (WS-9 review B6–B8; A-23) Prefixed recipe merges preserve the original namespace at each deferred parameter occurrence, including defaults, inline concept sets, window anchors, censor tags, population/output references and publication roots, through binding and serialization. A whole-source placeholder remains intact in generated advanced code. Parameterized zero washout generates the same criteria as literal zero. Base sharing is resolved after binding when necessary, using current population and source definitions and preserving edits made after merging. Generated advanced code preserves edited block members and provenance; simple new-user and study printing states the chosen washout and era defaults.

  • (WS-9 re-review R3–R4; A-23) Simple helpers defer numeric unit restrictions, new-user event selection and row-count expansion until parameter binding. Defaults, staged binding, prefixed merges and JSON/YAML/generated-code forms retain the literal helper’s plan, source options and user edits. Predicate serialization preserves numeric literal storage. Parameter arithmetic uses numeric intermediates, avoiding integer-storage overflow while retaining contextual integer validation and non-finite-expression refusals.

  • Large numeric literals and public cut boundaries use round-tripping JSON numbers in verb and plan transport, preserving distinct representable values beyond the range of exact consecutive doubles.

  • ds.omop.mutate() and ds.omop.filter(expr = ) check every participating site’s published protocol and verb method before any assignment, including an in-place mutation’s rollback copy. Old, incomplete or unavailable profiles refuse the whole call with the missing methods and upgrade advice; advertised verb capabilities alone do not bypass this check. The legacy var/op/value filter keeps its existing route.

  • Plan execution reads authenticated publication status before cleanup and uses the server inventory, including freshly allocated component symbols. Technical and transport failures revoke staged files as well as assigned outputs.

  • A partial out mapping without an explicit publish requests only the mapped outputs. For example, out = c(conditions = "cond_df") publishes only cond_df; the server leaves other computed outputs private and the client accepts the matching publication status.

  • (B-8) parent_id now restricts membership (see dsOMOP 2.10.3): a child population is a subset of its parent, as print() has always shown. A recipe with parent_id is compiled to a v2 plan and refused, naming population.parent, by servers that cannot apply it.

  • (F-3) The client blocklist is identical to the server’s class-1 patterns; birth components are not blocked on assignment paths. Informational quasi_identifier lint identifies birth, age and date variables without changing compilation or aggregate admission.

  • Circe imports carry their language-2 form: the first primary event that satisfies the observation window (select = "first_eligible" over omop_observed(before = PriorDays, after = PostDays), unique coverage), which is Circe’s own order; expressions with inclusion rules keep the 2.10.1 form.

  • Recipe JSON export and plan JSON save keep every digit (digits = NA) and YAML 15 significant digits: numbers such as unit conversion factors no longer round to 4 / 7 digits on export.

  • recipe_to_code() of a recipe with exactly one language-2 variable emitted variables = name = ..., which does not parse; it is list(name = ...).

  • A refused manipulation verb (ds.omop.merge(), ds.omop.filter(), ds.omop.select(), ds.omop.bind_rows(), ds.omop.mutate()) reports each server’s own reason – for a publication refusal its constant message – instead of the server names or DSI’s “There are some DataSHIELD errors”.

Newly permitted

  • (B-20) omop_index_event() accepts every event table of the server’s role registry (vendored inst/ohdsi/roles-5.3.csv, roles-5.4.csv): besides the seven tables of 2.10.2, visit_detail, observation_period, death, specimen, note, payer_plan_period, the era tables and episode; the server checks the table against its own CDM version.

  • on_small_site = "skip" on plan and recipe execution keeps successful sites while asking each server to commit all output families or none. Non-strict partial results warn with rejected family names and codes.

  • Numeric row thresholds and one-sided measurement criteria compile without safe bins; supplied bin contracts retain their scope checks. Removed the narrow_filter / unbound_numeric_filter lints and filter safety categories.

  • Circe round-trips one-sided measurement bounds with identical endpoint semantics; half-open two-sided ranges and authenticated bin contracts still refuse export because Circe cannot preserve them.

  • (F-17) omop_filter_date_range() accepts one-sided ranges (>= / <=).

  • (A-E5) -Inf is accepted as an unbounded window start and Inf as an unbounded end (also for a survival tar$end_offset); reversed infinities are errors.

  • Exact birth components and exact age may be requested in assigned tables (class 2, released only through the final minimum-persons rule).

  • (design 6.6) omop_filter_group(operator = "NOT") negates the conjunction of its children: the legacy spelling of omop_not().

  • (B-22) omop_output(type = "covariates_sparse") is the language-2 format = "sparse" over the output’s variables; format = "membership" and "dictionary" are reachable too.

  • (B-19) A feature output may mix variables with and without an index-relative window: one roster with one reducer window per variable; a windowed features output without an explicit grain takes episode grain (A-14/A-24) and needs an indexed population; an explicit incompatible grain (such as options = list(grain = "person")) keeps the ordinary v1 refusal, as does the corresponding wide grain refusal. An explicit episode grain retains v1 selection when the complete recipe is v1-expressible.

  • (design 2.2, 6.12) Survival outcomes and interval or temporal-covariate sources may be narrowed by visit or concept column; an intervals output may mix concept-scoped and unscoped variables of one table (one source per scope); a temporal-covariates output may declare different analyses per concept (per-source analyses, A-14).

  • These shapes have no v1 rendering: they run on dsOMOP 2.10.3 servers; recipe_lint() reports them as INFO language_2_only.

  • ds.omop.filter(expr = omop_where(...)) filters a server-side table with every comparison of the predicate grammar (< <= > >=, between, is.na(), !, &, |), three-valued; the legacy var/op/value form keeps ==, !=, in, not_in.

  • (F-1) New omop_filter_concept_set(concept_ids, concept_col = NULL): a row concept-set filter matching the output table’s domain concept column from the role registry (condition_concept_id for condition_occurrence, …), or concept_col. Row concept-set filters compiled to the column concept_id, which the server refused.

  • (A-18) The section 11 adapter refusals reach the analyst as the error Plan publication refused: <site>:<output> [validation_error] (<reason>) with adapter_person_mismatch or cost_currency_mixed, under both on_small_site settings (they are never skippable), and nothing is published; tested end to end through DSLite against a PostgreSQL CDM.

Newly refused

  • Adding a conflicting definition for an existing variable-block ID is refused; re-adding the identical definition leaves the recipe unchanged.
  • (F-2) A recipe-level row filter is attached only to outputs whose event table has every column it references; otherwise recipe_to_plan() stops naming the output and the missing column (the filter was attached to every output and failed at the server). Table-agnostic date and concept-set filters still apply to every output, and columns no CDM table defines are left to the server. Put the predicate on an omop_event(where = ...) of the right table instead.
  • Invalid or incomplete publication status fails closed; only insufficient_support can skip a site.
  • Plans that do not validate against the vendored plan-v2.json are never sent; a v2 recipe whose operations an older server lacks is refused with the operation named (parent inheritance, coverage policies, event censoring and matching are never dropped to fit an older server).
  • recipe_to_plan(version = 1) refuses language-2 constructs, naming them.
  • A language-2 survival output needs an explicit censor list; class-1 columns are refused at compile time in projections, value columns and predicates of v2 plans.

Shared with dsOMOP 2.10.3 (WS-2)

  • The language 2.0 normal form is the frozen, byte-identically vendored R/plan_normalize_v2.R (.planNormalizeV2(), amendment A-11); the server’s .irNormalize() calls the same function, so normalised forms and semantic digests agree on both sides. WS-2’s interim R/ir_defaults.R (.irNormalizeWire()) is removed.
  • The role-registry tables (inst/ohdsi/roles-5.3.csv, roles-5.4.csv) are vendored byte-identically from dsOMOP.

Upgrading clients and servers

  • Before anything is assigned, every execution checks the methods each site’s profile publishes (review B1). With every site on dsOMOP 2.10.3 the publication protocol runs (omopPlanStatusDS, omopStagedRevokeDS, commit_policy). While any site lacks it, a language-2 plan is refused before any assignment, naming the sites, the missing methods and the required installed/published version (dsOMOP 2.10.3). A v1-selected recipe or plan then runs on every site as the legacy call of dsOMOPClient 2.10.2 (the same v1 payload, no commit_policy, no status or revocation calls) with one warning naming the old sites: on_small_site does not change that legacy call; cross-site rollback and the section 7.3 publication guarantees do not apply until they upgrade, and each server applies its own disclosure rules. DP preparation and the sticky query library follow the same rule. A site whose profile cannot be listed, or that lacks a method the call needs on either route, stops the execution before anything is sent. ds.omop.server.version() reports both installed and published versions; an Opal profile retains its previous methods until publication.
  • With a 2.10.1 or 2.10.2 client and a 2.10.3 server, a strict publication refusal still publishes nothing. The assign call returns status refused, and the old client then reports that requested outputs did not materialize instead of receiving the previous constant Disclosive error.

Contracts shipped by WS-0

  • Vendored inst/schema/ (byte-identical to dsOMOP’s), R/json_schema.R, R/semantic_digest.R; openssl added to Imports for the semantic digest. The digest’s number serialisation finds the ECMAScript shortest round-trip decimal for every finite double (power-of-two regression 2^-24 -> 5.960464477539063e-8; digest vector power_of_two_factor).
  • Vendored R/plan_normalize_v2.R (amendment A-11): .planNormalizeV2() is the one normal form the semantic digest hashes on client and server; the normalised fixtures of inst/schema/normalized/ are pinned. plan-v2.json gains source_analyses on temporal and person-period outputs (A-14). The vendored probe corpus carries the A-15/A-16 IR-only variants, refused on the wire (P64-P66).
  • A-18 .plan_validate_status() admits the optional closed reason of a rejected entry (only with validation_error); the refusal diagnostic names it with the output and code (site:output [validation_error] (reason)). Amendment A-20 (j) adds stockpile_row_cap and reducer_row_cap (the server’s bounded interval realisations) to the vocabulary.

dsOMOPClient 2.10.2

  • Version aligned with dsOMOP 2.10.2 (which reads every OMOP CDM version label); no client change.

dsOMOPClient 2.10.1

  • ds.omop.connect() reports each server’s own error instead of DSI’s generic “There are some DataSHIELD errors, list them with datashield.errors()”, followed by what to do when that is known. A server whose DataSHIELD profile does not publish dsOMOP’s methods (dsOMOP missing, or upgraded on Opal without publishing its settings again) now stops the connection before anything is assigned, naming the missing method and the Opal page where an administrator publishes it.
  • New ds.omop.client.version(): the installed dsOMOPClient version.
  • New ds.omop.server.version(conns): works on plain DataSHIELD connections, before ds.omop.connect(). Per server it reports the dsOMOP version whose methods the profile publishes, the version that answers (the installed one), the methods this client calls that the profile lacks, whether the server is ready, and what to change when it is not.
  • Pairs with dsOMOP 2.10.1, which never requires TLS on a database connection, reads dsOMOP 1.x resources and finds the CDM schema of a resource that names none.

dsOMOPClient 2.10.0

  • Support dsOMOP 2.10.0’s seed-only DP: servers reporting release_binding = "seed_data_versioned_v1" (no stored answers; answers are deterministic from the server’s secret root, the question and the data) are accepted for ds.omop.dp.release() and the sticky QueryLibrary releases, alone or mixed with first-answer servers (dsOMOP 2.7.1 to 2.9.x). mixed_contracts now also reports such a mix. The seed stays entirely server-side; the client only learns the new contract label.
  • Help pages, README and vignettes describe both server generations; an incoherent v3 status is now reported as “incoherent v3 DP contract”.

dsOMOPClient 2.9.1

  • New ds.omop.dp.prepare(): prepares a person-local table for sticky DP releases from an omop_recipe or omop_plan (server method omopDpPlanExecuteDS, dsOMOP 2.9.1). Loading tables with ds.omop.plan.execute() and recipe_execute() is unchanged and never uses DP. Prepared tables skip concept-factor harmonization, which would drop the DP seal.
  • ds.omop.querylibrary.sticky.release() works in one call: without x it prepares the input from the redesign’s preparation recipe or plan into a temporary server symbol, releases, and removes it. The redesign can be the first argument.
  • omop_querylibrary_sticky_catalog() gains automatic_equivalent: the analysis-catalog entry that answers the question with no preparation (dsOMOP 2.9.0), also shown when a redesign is printed and suggested when a release has no input.
  • Plan execution errors now include each server’s own reason.

dsOMOPClient 2.9.0

  • Support dsOMOP 2.9.0’s automatic protection of the OHDSI community tools. ds.omop.analysis.run() keeps each server’s protection label in meta$protection ("standard", "dp" with epsilon, sensitivity and the noise standard deviation, or "standard_fallback"), and the result prints it with the estimand. ds.omop.query.exec() keeps the labels in the dsomop.protection attribute.
  • The reopened query-library questions (per-person durations and counts, demographic distributions, values, quantities and costs) pool through their server-owned contracts like every other analysis.
  • When federated analysis metadata differ because servers use different dsomop.tools.mode settings, the error names each server’s mode.
  • ds.omop.dp.status() prints each server’s tools mode.
  • Documentation: sticky QueryLibrary redesigns take their input from a community-tool loader (an assign-mode analysis-catalog entry), because plan and recipe outputs carry no DP provenance since dsOMOP 2.8.0; the common per-person questions need no preparation in 2.9.0.

dsOMOPClient 2.8.0

  • Loading tables never depends on differential privacy (DP). ds.omop.plan.execute() no longer requests DP status before execution and always performs the requested concept-factor harmonization, as before DP was added. Servers 2.7.x with exclusive DP refuse factor discovery: set factor_concepts = FALSE there, or upgrade them to dsOMOP 2.8.0.
  • The shared aggregate helper no longer turns DP-exclusive refusals into a special fatal error. It reports clearly when a server has the OHDSI community tools disabled (dsomop.tools.enabled), and analysis failures now include each server’s reason.

dsOMOPClient 2.7.4

  • Support dsOMOP 2.7.1’s v3 snapshot-first-answer contract for isglobal-brge/dsOMOP#20. Validate the persistent binding and public storage-capacity status fields, and include them in federation compatibility and result metadata.
  • Keep legacy v2 status inspectable and explicitly labelled as old. Release calls require the new contract by default. The opt-in client option dsomop.dp.allow_legacy_servers = TRUE supports staged upgrades, including mixed v2/v3 federations, with a warning naming every legacy server: no first-answer binding: an unrotated data refresh can reveal whether a released statistic changed; see isglobal-brge/dsOMOP#20. Results retain each server’s contract and legacy warnings, including pooled-only views; shared contract fields that differ across sites are NULL. All mechanism, provenance, harmonization and per-site payload checks remain in force.
  • Document permanent first answers, stale-until-custodian-rotation semantics, automatic server-store initialization with a local identity pin, recommended external pinning, persistent state recovery and the default 1 GiB public reservation capacity. All seven primitive calculations, sensitivities, epsilon/delta and pooling formulas remain unchanged.

dsOMOPClient 2.7.3

  • Adapt memory-mode plan and recipe execution to dsOMOP 2.7.0’s default exclusive DP channel: automatically disable observed factor-level discovery across the selected federation with an explanatory message.
  • Validate and print the DP status’s exclusive flag, retaining compatibility with dsOMOP 2.6.0, which omits it.
  • Standard statistics helpers now surface exclusive-mode refusals as clear errors directing analysts to ds.omop.dp.release(); no partial standard result is returned when a selected server refuses the channel.

dsOMOPClient 2.7.2

  • Document the server 2.6.0 default-enabled DP release channel, custodial opt-out, derived resource/snapshot identities, privacy epoch and persistent state requirements. Client release calls remain explicit; no API defaults change.
